settings.description: Base URL of the Frontier server (for example https://frontier.example.com). Empty means offline: runs are recorded locally and synced later.
settings.title: Control plane URL

settings.description: Where the SDK writes run records when no server is reachable. Relative paths are relative to the working directory.
settings.title: Offline run directory

settings.description: Timeout of one request to the control plane.
settings.title: Request timeout (seconds)

settings.description: Where converted frontier-datasets go. On a server, when set: cases converted on the Connectors page (`<dir>/converted/<name>`) and hub pulls (`<dir>/hub/<id>`) are written here instead of the server's data directory.
settings.title: Datasets directory

settings.description: Where `frontier hub pull` stores files as published, one sub-directory per dataset. Relative paths are relative to the working directory.
settings.title: Raw downloads directory

settings.description: Downloads that can be fetched again (cloud-solver results, plugin wheels).
settings.title: Cache directory

settings.description: Where local runs write checkpoints, logs and reports. Relative paths are relative to the working directory.
settings.title: Run output directory

settings.description: Directories under which a request may name a path for the server to read or write (registering a dataset, trying a connector, a hub pull target). The data directory and `storage.datasets_dir` always count. Empty: no further restriction in single-user mode; with authentication on, only those two.
settings.title: Directories the server may read on request

settings.description: Largest pull that starts without --yes or an explicit --max-bytes.
settings.title: Download size limit

settings.description: Replaces the built-in hub catalogue (a catalog.json exported by `frontier hub export`). Empty uses the built-in one.
settings.title: Catalogue file

settings.description: Directories or files with more catalogue entries (an organisation's internal datasets).
settings.title: Additional catalogues

settings.description: Where your organisation keeps raw files of hub entries: items `<entry id or pattern>=<location>`, first match wins, for example `shift-*=s3://company-datasets/restricted` and `*=/mnt/datasets/hub`. A location is a directory or an object-store prefix (s3://, r2://, gs://, az://). Credentials for it come from the secret store (providers `s3`, `gcs`, `azure`), never from the location.
settings.title: Organisation mirrors

settings.description: Base URL of a Hugging Face mirror (HF_ENDPOINT). Empty uses https://huggingface.co.
settings.title: Hugging Face endpoint

settings.description: Where `frontier run` sends a run when --on is not given.
settings.title: Default target

settings.description: Provider used by `frontier cloud up` and `frontier cloud offers` when --provider is not given.
settings.title: Default cloud provider

settings.description: GPU type `frontier cloud up` rents when --gpu is not given.
settings.title: Default GPU type

settings.description: RunPod capacity tier: `secure` (datacentre) or `community` (cheaper, interruptible hosts).
settings.title: Default cloud tier

settings.description: A cloud run is stopped when its accumulated cost reaches this amount, unless --max-cost says otherwise. 0 means no ceiling of your own; `policy.max_cost_per_run` caps it organisation-wide.
settings.title: Cost ceiling per run (USD)

settings.description: Registry and path the Frontier images are pulled from. The training image is `<registry>/frontier-trainer:<version>` and the server and worker image `<registry>/frontier:<version>`.
settings.title: Container registry

settings.description: Container image a run uses on cloud, SLURM and Kubernetes targets. Empty uses `<compute.registry>/frontier-trainer:<version>`.
settings.title: Training image

settings.description: Container image `frontier cloud up` starts on a rented instance. Empty uses `<compute.registry>/frontier:<version>`.
settings.title: Worker image

settings.description: Python interpreter (or command prefix) that has the Frontier Python packages. Empty uses `.venv` in the project directory, then `uv run python`.
settings.title: Python interpreter

settings.description: Named sets of devices with a role mask, `[compute.pools.<name>]` with `nodes`, `gpus`, `roles` (training, inference, rendering, prep, any), `quota` (`{gpus, jobs}`), `priority`, `shared` and `description`. Every device not named by a pool belongs to the built-in `auto` pool with all roles.
settings.title: Compute pools

settings.description: Pool the control plane's render workers (thumbnails, render-to-image, frame preparation) take their device from. Empty = any pool that serves the `rendering` role, `auto` included.
settings.title: Rendering pool

settings.description: How devices are picked for a job inside a pool: `topology` (same node first, NVLink islands for multi-GPU jobs, then least loaded), `least_loaded` (lowest utilisation and memory use first) or `memory_fit` (the smallest device that fits the request).
settings.title: Allocation policy

settings.description: Start a `frontier-worker` for the `local` backend next to the control plane, so a single-machine install runs jobs without starting a worker by hand. Turn it off on shared servers where workers run on other machines.
settings.title: Built-in local worker

settings.description: How many jobs the built-in local worker runs at the same time. Two lets an inference predict while a model trains on the same machine; 1 runs them one after the other.
settings.title: Jobs of the built-in worker

settings.description: How many predictions made by an automatic rule (a new checkpoint, a schedule) are kept for one Inference node; older ones are removed with their files. Predictions a person asked for are never removed. 0 keeps all.
settings.title: Automatic predictions kept per node

settings.description: How many requests the runtime of a served board answers at the same time; the rest wait. A service can set its own.
settings.title: Requests a service answers at once

settings.description: A running service that took no request for this long is stopped and its worker released; the next call starts it again and waits for it. 0 keeps services running.
settings.title: Release an idle service after (minutes)

settings.description: At most this many calls per minute to one service; more are refused with 429. A service can set its own.
settings.title: Requests per minute per service

settings.description: A call with a larger body is refused with 413. A service can set its own.
settings.title: Largest request to a service (MB)

settings.description: An allocation is released when no heartbeat from its worker renews it for this long, and its job is marked failed (`worker lost`).
settings.title: Allocation lease (seconds)

settings.description: Site profile (a file in the `sites` directory of the Frontier home) used by --on slurm / --on ssh when neither --site nor --host is given.
settings.title: Default site profile

settings.description: Partition for generated batch scripts when the site profile does not set one.
settings.title: Partition

settings.description: Accounting project for generated batch scripts when the site profile does not set one.
settings.title: Account

settings.description: Wall-clock limit (HH:MM:SS) of a generated worker allocation.
settings.title: Time limit

settings.description: Python package index plugins are installed from. Empty uses the installer's default (PyPI). Set it to an internal mirror in restricted networks.
settings.title: Package index

settings.description: Directory of plugin wheels to install from instead of an index (air-gapped installations). When set, no index is contacted.
settings.title: Wheel directory

settings.description: Tool that installs plugin wheels: uv when available, else pip.
settings.title: Installer

settings.description: Proxy for outbound HTTPS (exported to child processes as HTTPS_PROXY).
settings.title: HTTPS proxy

settings.description: Proxy for outbound HTTP (exported as HTTP_PROXY).
settings.title: HTTP proxy

settings.description: Hosts and domains reached directly (exported as NO_PROXY).
settings.title: Proxy exceptions

settings.description: PEM file with the certificate authorities to trust, for TLS-inspecting proxies and internal services (exported as SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and CURL_CA_BUNDLE).
settings.title: CA bundle

settings.description: Never open a connection to the public internet: hub pulls, plugin index lookups, price lists and update checks fail fast with an explanation instead of timing out.
settings.title: Offline mode

settings.description: Host names inside your network that stay reachable with `network.offline` on, besides this machine, private address ranges and the control plane (`client.server_url`): a secret manager, an identity provider, an internal package index.
settings.title: Hosts reachable in offline mode

settings.description: Where credentials are kept on this machine: the OS keychain, a 0600 file (`credentials.toml` in the state directory, for headless nodes), the environment only, or your organisation's secret manager: `vault` (HashiCorp Vault KV v2, `secrets.vault.*`), `aws` (AWS Secrets Manager, `secrets.aws.*`), `azure` (Azure Key Vault, `secrets.azure.*`) or `gcp` (Google Secret Manager, `secrets.gcp.*`). `auto` uses the keychain when one is available, else the file.
settings.title: Secret store

settings.description: Where the control plane keeps the credentials people store on it: `db` (its own database, each value encrypted with the server key), `vault` (HashiCorp Vault, `secrets.vault.*`) or `aws` (AWS Secrets Manager, `secrets.aws.*`). New and changed credentials go to this store; `POST /api/v1/secrets/backend/migrate` moves the existing ones.
settings.title: Control plane credential store

settings.description: How the key that encrypts the `db` credential store is kept: `file` (the key itself in `secrets.key_file`, or `FRONTIER_SECRET_KEY`) or `aws-kms` (envelope encryption: the file holds a data key wrapped by the KMS key `secrets.aws.kms_key_id`, unwrapped at start-up).
settings.title: Control plane key protection

settings.description: Address of the HashiCorp Vault server, for example https://vault.example.com:8200.
settings.title: Vault address

settings.description: Mount point of the KV version 2 secrets engine.
settings.title: Vault KV mount

settings.description: Path under the mount; one secret per credential provider is kept at `<prefix>/<provider>`, with one key per field.
settings.title: Vault path prefix

settings.description: Vault Enterprise / HCP namespace; empty for none.
settings.title: Vault namespace

settings.description: `token` (from `VAULT_TOKEN` or the credential file), `approle` (role id in `secrets.vault.role`, secret id from `FRONTIER_VAULT_SECRET_ID` or the credential file) or `kubernetes` (the pod's service-account token; role in `secrets.vault.role`).
settings.title: Vault authentication

settings.description: AppRole role id, or the role name of the Kubernetes auth method.
settings.title: Vault role

settings.description: Mount point of the auth method when it is not the default (`approle`, `kubernetes`).
settings.title: Vault auth mount

settings.description: File holding the Vault token or the AppRole secret id (or, for `kubernetes`, the service-account token when it is not at the standard path). Never put the value itself in a setting.
settings.title: Vault credential file

settings.description: Address of the key vault, for example https://frontier-prod.vault.azure.net.
settings.title: Azure Key Vault URL

settings.description: One secret per credential provider is kept as `<prefix>-<provider>` (Key Vault names allow letters, digits and dashes), a JSON object with one key per field.
settings.title: Azure secret name prefix

settings.description: `managed_identity` (the identity of the VM, container or AKS pod) or `client_secret` (an app registration: `secrets.azure.tenant_id`, `secrets.azure.client_id`, and the secret from `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` or `secrets.azure.credential_file`).
settings.title: Azure authentication

settings.description: Directory (tenant) id for `client_secret` authentication; empty uses `AZURE_TENANT_ID`.
settings.title: Azure tenant

settings.description: Application (client) id for `client_secret` authentication, or the client id of a user-assigned managed identity; empty uses `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`.
settings.title: Azure client id

settings.description: File holding the client secret. Never put the value itself in a setting.
settings.title: Azure credential file

settings.description: Token endpoint host when it is not https://login.microsoftonline.com (sovereign clouds, or an emulator in tests).
settings.title: Azure authority override

settings.description: Project id that holds the secrets; empty uses `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`.
settings.title: Google Cloud project

settings.description: One secret per credential provider is kept as `<prefix>-<provider>`, a JSON object with one key per field.
settings.title: Google secret id prefix

settings.description: `metadata` (the service account of the VM, Cloud Run service or GKE workload identity) or `service_account` (a key file: `secrets.gcp.credential_file`, or `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`).
settings.title: Google authentication

settings.description: JSON key file of the service account for `service_account` authentication.
settings.title: Google service-account key file

settings.description: Endpoint when it is not https://secretmanager.googleapis.com (Private Service Connect, or an emulator in tests).
settings.title: Google Secret Manager endpoint override

settings.description: Region of AWS Secrets Manager; empty uses `AWS_REGION`. Credentials come from `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (/ `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`) in the environment.
settings.title: AWS region

settings.description: One secret per credential provider is kept as `<prefix>/<provider>`, a JSON object with one key per field.
settings.title: AWS secret name prefix

settings.description: KMS key id, ARN or alias that new secrets are encrypted under; empty uses the account's default key for Secrets Manager.
settings.title: AWS KMS key

settings.description: Endpoint of KMS when it is not the public one: a VPC endpoint, or an emulator in tests.
settings.title: AWS KMS endpoint override

settings.description: Endpoint of Secrets Manager when it is not the public one: a VPC endpoint, or an emulator in tests.
settings.title: AWS endpoint override

settings.description: File with the 32-byte key (hex or base64) that encrypts credentials stored by the server. FRONTIER_SECRET_KEY takes precedence. Empty uses `secret.key` in the server data directory, created on first start.
settings.title: Server encryption key file

settings.description: Verbosity of every Frontier process. RUST_LOG, when set, still wins for the Rust binaries.
settings.title: Log level

settings.description: `json` writes one JSON object per line for log collectors.
settings.title: Log format

settings.description: Colour theme of the app and the TUI.
settings.title: Theme

settings.description: Unit system used when displaying physical quantities.
settings.title: Units

settings.description: Colour map applied to a scalar field when none was chosen.
settings.title: Default colour map

settings.description: How often the TUI and live views poll for new data.
settings.title: Refresh interval (ms)

settings.description: `follow`: the object follows the hand when you drag, and rolling the wheel away from you zooms in, as in ParaView. `camera`: drags move the camera instead. `custom`: the three switches below.
settings.title: Navigation style

settings.description: With navigation style `custom`: a drag to the left turns the object to the right.
settings.title: Invert horizontal orbit

settings.description: With navigation style `custom`: a drag down turns the object up.
settings.title: Invert vertical orbit

settings.description: With navigation style `custom`: rolling the wheel away from you zooms out.
settings.title: Invert zoom

settings.description: Pointer shown over a 3D or 2D view while it reads the value under it. Dragging always shows the grabbing hand.
settings.title: Probe cursor

settings.description: `follow`: light or dark with the app. `light` or `dark`: always that one.
settings.title: Editor theme

settings.description: `default`: the app's palette. `vivid`: stronger colours. `quiet`: keys and strings only; everything else in the text colour.
settings.title: Syntax colours

settings.description: Size of the editor's text at 100% zoom.
settings.title: Font size (px)

settings.description: Height of a row as a multiple of the font size.
settings.title: Line height

settings.description: Cells a tab stop spans, and spaces one press of Tab inserts.
settings.title: Tab size

settings.description: Tab inserts spaces up to the next tab stop. Off: a tab character.
settings.title: Indent with spaces

settings.description: Long lines continue on the next row instead of scrolling sideways. A node's own Wrap lines setting wins.
settings.title: Wrap lines

settings.description: Show the number of each line beside it.
settings.title: Line numbers

settings.description: An outline of the whole file beside the scrollbar, when the editor is wide enough for it.
settings.title: Minimap

settings.description: Tint the row the caret is on.
settings.title: Highlight the current line

settings.description: Shape of the caret.
settings.title: Cursor

settings.description: Off: the caret is always shown.
settings.title: Blinking cursor

settings.description: Typing an opening bracket or quote inserts its pair.
settings.title: Close brackets and quotes

settings.description: Saving a JSON, YAML or TOML file formats it first. Comments and values are kept; a file with a syntax error is saved as it is.
settings.title: Format on save

settings.description: Corner of the window where toasts appear. They never cover the top bar or a board's toolbar.
settings.title: Toast position

settings.description: How long an information or success toast stays. Warnings and errors stay until dismissed.
settings.title: Toast duration (s)

settings.description: More than this collapse into a count that opens the notification centre.
settings.title: Toasts shown at once

settings.description: Play a short sound with a warning or an error toast.
settings.title: Sound

settings.description: Show no toasts; everything still arrives in the notification centre.
settings.title: Do not disturb

settings.description: `mine`: only what you started. `projects`: everything in the projects you may read.
settings.title: Whose events

settings.description: Also show a notification of the operating system (the browser asks for permission) while the window is not in front.
settings.title: System notifications

settings.description: A pipeline run or a training run finished or failed. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Runs

settings.description: A step of a pipeline run failed. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Pipeline steps

settings.description: A job failed, or has been queued for a long time. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Jobs

settings.description: A dataset import or a data-preparation step finished. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Datasets

settings.description: An evaluation finished, a report is ready, or a quality gate refused a model. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Evaluations and reports

settings.description: A model version changed stage or was deployed. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Models

settings.description: A data-preparation step or an AI agent's plan waits for a decision, or was approved or refused. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Approvals

settings.description: A worker went offline, a pool has no capacity, or a cloud pod is about to be released. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Compute

settings.description: Spending reached a threshold. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Cost

settings.description: A credential expires soon or failed its test. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Credentials

settings.description: The app lost its server or reached it again. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Connection

settings.description: A newer version of Frontier is available. `toast`: a toast and an entry in the notification centre. `centre`: the entry only. `off`: nothing.
settings.title: Updates

settings.description: Address and port the control plane listens on.
settings.title: Listen address

settings.description: SQLite database of the control plane.
settings.title: Database file

settings.description: Artifacts, job logs and hub pulls of the control plane.
settings.title: Data directory

settings.description: Origins allowed to call the API besides localhost and the desktop app (for example https://frontier.example.com).
settings.title: Additional browser origins

settings.description: Host names this server answers to besides localhost and the hosts of `server.cors_origins` (the public DNS name behind a proxy, a pod's proxy host). Requests with another `Host` are refused, which is what stops DNS rebinding. `*` accepts any host: only with authentication on.
settings.title: Accepted Host names

settings.description: Hand credentials stored on the server to the jobs that ask for them when a worker claims the job. When off, jobs only see what the worker's own environment provides.
settings.title: Give credentials to jobs

settings.description: `none`: single-user, every request acts as the local administrator (only on a loopback address). `token`: API tokens. `oidc`: people sign in through an OpenID Connect provider; the CLI, workers and CI use API tokens.
settings.title: Authentication mode

settings.description: Let the server start with `auth.mode = "none"` on an address other machines can reach. Everyone who can connect is then an administrator.
settings.title: Allow single-user mode on the network

settings.description: With `auth.mode = "none"`, every request that changes something or touches credentials must carry the token the server writes at start-up to `<data dir>/local-token` and `~/.frontier/servers/<port>.token` (owner-readable only). The CLI, the SDK and workers on this machine read it by themselves; the browser app obtains it from `POST /api/v1/auth/local-session`. Turning it off lets every local process and every allowed web origin act as administrator.
settings.title: Require the local token in single-user mode

settings.description: Let the server listen on an address other machines can reach although `auth.public_url` is not an https URL. Set it when TLS ends at a reverse proxy you have not described in `auth.public_url`, or on a network you trust with tokens in clear.
settings.title: Allow a network address without TLS

settings.description: Let the person who submitted a data-preparation run or started an agent session also approve it. Off: an approval is a second person's decision (four-eyes); on, for teams with a single reviewer.
settings.title: Allow approving one's own plans

settings.description: How long a browser session stays valid after sign-in.
settings.title: Session lifetime (hours)

settings.description: Lifetime of a new API token when none is asked for; 0 means it does not expire.
settings.title: Default API token lifetime (days)

settings.description: Upper bound for the lifetime of tokens people create for themselves; 0 means no bound. Service-account tokens issued by an administrator are not bound by it.
settings.title: Longest API token lifetime (days)

settings.description: The address browsers reach the server at (for example https://frontier.example.com); the OIDC redirect URI is `<public_url>/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback`. Empty: derived from the listen address.
settings.title: Public URL of the control plane

settings.description: Record the client address a reverse proxy reports instead of the proxy's own. Enable only behind a proxy that overwrites the header.
settings.title: Trust X-Forwarded-For

settings.description: Audit records older than this are removed at start-up and daily; the chain stays verifiable from a recorded anchor. 0 keeps everything.
settings.title: Audit log retention (days)

settings.description: Issuer URL of the identity provider; `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` must exist.
settings.title: OIDC issuer

settings.description: Client id registered for Frontier at the provider. The client secret, if the provider issues one, is the credential `frontier-oidc` (or `FRONTIER_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`), never a setting.
settings.title: OIDC client id

settings.description: Scopes requested at sign-in; add the one that makes the provider include groups (often `groups`).
settings.title: OIDC scopes

settings.description: Claim used as the Frontier login name; falls back to `email`, then `sub`.
settings.title: Login name claim

settings.description: Claim listing the user's groups (an array or a space-separated string; dots descend, as in `realm_access.roles`).
settings.title: Groups claim

settings.description: Group name to `admin`, `maintainer`, `member`, `viewer` or `auditor` (organisation role), or `project:<project name>:<role>`. The highest matching role applies and is re-evaluated at every sign-in.
settings.title: Group to role mapping

settings.description: Organisation role of a user none of whose groups is mapped; empty refuses the sign-in.
settings.title: Role without a mapped group

settings.description: Which jobs this worker claims.
settings.title: Backend

settings.description: Labels this worker advertises (`gpu=h100`, `site=eu`); a job is claimed only by a worker with all of its labels.
settings.title: Labels

settings.description: How often the worker reports to the control plane and asks for work.
settings.title: Heartbeat interval (seconds)

settings.description: Directory jobs run in when they do not name one.
settings.title: Working directory

settings.description: Run a job's image with Docker instead of as a bare process.
settings.title: Run jobs in containers

settings.description: Names of environment variables of the worker process that jobs inherit, besides the basic ones (PATH, HOME, locale, temporary directory, CUDA/NVIDIA, Python and proxy variables). A job never inherits the worker's token or any other variable by default: what it needs comes with the job.
settings.title: Worker variables jobs may see

settings.description: Operating-system user jobs are started as when the worker runs as root (containers, system services), so a job cannot read the worker's files or signal it. Empty runs jobs as the worker's own user.
settings.title: User that jobs run as

settings.description: Time a cancelled job gets between SIGTERM and SIGKILL. The job uses it to stop its step and to pack and upload what it produced (checkpoints, metrics, evaluation files).
settings.title: Termination grace (seconds)

settings.description: Largest JSON request (metric batches, job logs) the control plane accepts. Artifact uploads are streamed and not limited by this.
settings.title: Request size limit

settings.description: Upper bound on one uploaded run artifact (checkpoints, prediction stores, model packages). A larger upload is cut off and removed.
settings.title: Largest artifact upload

settings.description: Upper bound on the total size of one run's artifacts; an upload that would exceed it is refused. 0 means no bound.
settings.title: Artifact space per run

settings.description: Uploads are refused while the data directory's file system has less free space than this, so the database and job logs can still be written. 0 turns the check off.
settings.title: Free disk space to keep

settings.description: A request whose handler has not answered after this long is ended with 504. Event streams and downloads are not cut (they answer at once and then stream); artifact uploads are exempt. 0 means no timeout.
settings.title: Request timeout (seconds)

settings.description: Live event streams (run events, agent sessions, model events) one caller may hold open at a time; further ones are refused with 429. 0 means no bound.
settings.title: Event streams per client

settings.description: Requests the control plane works on at once, open event streams included; further ones wait.
settings.title: Concurrent requests

settings.description: After this many rejected tokens, sessions or sign-ins from one address within a minute, further rejected attempts from it are answered 429 and no longer written to the audit log until the minute has passed. Valid credentials keep working. 0 turns the limit off.
settings.title: Rejected sign-ins per minute and address

settings.description: Upper bound on the memory one read of a dataset or prediction array may need. A store whose metadata declares more is refused instead of loaded, so a hostile or corrupt upload cannot exhaust the server's memory.
settings.title: Largest array read at once

settings.description: Targets runs may be sent to. Remove `runpod` and `anyscale` to keep every run on your own machines.
settings.title: Allowed compute targets

settings.description: When off, `frontier hub pull` and the app refuse to download from public hosts; only catalogue entries served from `hub.extra_catalogs` on local paths remain available.
settings.title: Allow public dataset downloads

settings.description: Which hub datasets may be pulled: `any`, `commercial` (licences that permit commercial use), or SPDX identifiers (for example CC-BY-4.0). A dataset must match at least one entry.
settings.title: Allowed dataset licences

settings.description: Upper bound for the cost ceiling of any cloud run or sweep. 0 means no organisation-wide ceiling.
settings.title: Cost ceiling per run (USD)

settings.description: When off, the set of plugins is frozen: nobody can install, uninstall, enable or disable a plugin or deploy an exporter from the CLI or the app. Administrators change plugins by changing the installation.
settings.title: Allow plugin changes

settings.description: Where plugins may be installed from: `bundled` (shipped with the product), `pypi` (the official index), `index` (the configured `plugins.index_url`), `wheel_dir` (the configured wheel directory), a URL or path prefix, or `any`. The default is the official index plus what an administrator configured; a path, wheel or URL named on a command line needs its prefix listed here (or `any`).
settings.title: Allowed plugin sources

settings.description: Pools a run or job may ask for: `any`, or pool names. A job that names another pool is refused; `auto` always resolves inside the allowed pools.
settings.title: Allowed compute pools

settings.description: Largest number of GPUs (over all nodes) one run or job may hold. 0 means no organisation-wide ceiling.
settings.title: GPUs per run (ceiling)

settings.description: Provider ids an agent session or a judge may use: `local` (covers `ollama`, `vllm`, `llamacpp`, `rules`, `nli`), `anthropic`, `openai`, `typesafe`, or `any`.
settings.title: Allowed model providers

settings.description: When off, every hosted model provider (anthropic, openai, typesafe) is refused whatever `allowed_providers` says: plan and preview summaries would be sent off-site.
settings.title: Allow data to leave the site

settings.description: Operation classes (`prep.fields`, `prep.samples.drop`, `all`) an agent may `run` without a person's approval. Empty means every run needs an approval.
settings.title: Op classes an agent may run unattended

settings.description: Who may change the settings a server reads when it starts (listen address, sign-in mode, limits, the secret store) through the API, the app and `frontier config set --on-server`, and restart it from there. `local`: only in single-user mode from this machine, written to the server's own config file. `admin`: any administrator who is signed in. `off`: only by editing the config file.
settings.title: Start-up settings from the app

settings.description: When on, an inference may send a signed POST to a URL when its predictions are ready (`notify` in the API, "Notify URL" on an Inference node). The request carries ids and links, never arrays.
settings.title: Allow inference webhooks

settings.description: Host names a notify URL may point at. Empty means any host, once webhooks are allowed.
settings.title: Hosts an inference may notify

settings.description: `auto` picks TypeSafe when allowed and configured, else the local model when its endpoint answers, else rules; or name one of `local`, `rules`, `nli`, `typesafe`.
settings.title: Judge backend

settings.description: The local model server (Ollama native API; an endpoint ending in `/v1` is treated as OpenAI-compatible: vLLM, llama.cpp server).
settings.title: Local model endpoint

settings.description: Host names (or `host:port`) besides this machine that the provider `local` may reach: a model server inside the site's network. Anything else is treated as data leaving the site. Read from the system file and the control plane only.
settings.title: Hosts that count as local model servers

settings.description: Model tag on the local endpoint used for judgments and local agent sessions.
settings.title: Local model

settings.description: The hosted provider for `--hosted` sessions (needs `data_leaves_site` and a credential: `frontier auth login anthropic`).
settings.title: Hosted provider

settings.description: Model id at the hosted provider for `--hosted` sessions.
settings.title: Hosted model

settings.description: Budget of tool calls one agent session may make.
settings.title: Tool calls per session

settings.description: Where session records (`<id>.jsonl`: every tool call, preview, judgment and approval) are written.
settings.title: Session record directory
